title: Manchester City left unhappy with 3 games in 7 days after Premier League fixture rescheduling
content:
Manchester City are frustrated with changes to the Premier League fixture schedule that will see them play three matches in seven days during their title run-in.

The Premier League announced the dates of its rearranged fixtures on Tuesday.

Two of City’s remaining five Premier League fixtures, against Bournemouth and Crystal Palace, needed rescheduling after Pep Guardiola’s side reached both domestic cup finals, leaving them with a packed schedule in May.

The Premier League has confirmed that City will host Palace on Wednesday, May 13 at 8pm BST, with their visit to Bournemouth scheduled for Tuesday, May 19 at 7.30pm BST – either side of the FA Cup final against Chelsea on Sunday, May 16.

City were due to play Bournemouth on the weekend of the showpiece at Wembley, while the Palace game was moved because it was initially scheduled for the weekend of March 21-22 – when City beat Arsenal in the Carabao Cup final.

Palace have Conference League commitments of their own, with a two-legged semi-final against Shakhtar Donetsk next month, meaning they could not play City during the week starting May 4.

Meanwhile, UEFA, the European governing body, did not want the Bournemouth game to clash with the Europa League final on May 20 – particularly as one of Aston Villa or Nottingham Forest will feature.

City are three points behind league leaders Arsenal with a game in hand, and play after Mikel Arteta’s side this weekend.

Analysis by Manchester City correspondent Sam Lee

City are annoyed about the late season schedule for various reasons: for having to play three games in the space of seven days, because they provided several alternatives and because they believe the Premier League have had plenty of time to have sorted this out before now.

It became clear on February 4, when City progressed to the Carabao Cup final, that the game against Crystal Palace, scheduled for the weekend of the final, would not be able to go ahead as scheduled.

City believe that the principle of rescheduling games for the earliest possible moment has not been followed in the case of the Palace fixture, compared to their game against Burnley, which clashed with the FA Cup semi-final and was swiftly brought forward.

City had proposed to play the away game at Bournemouth on May 12 and to welcome Palace at home a week later, which would have given them two home games to finish the season.

There has been a considerable amount of negotiation regarding the order and exact date of the fixtures going back weeks.

There is a flavour of the ongoing enmity between City and the Premier League during these discussions; the Premier League have referenced a principle that all FA Cup semi-finalists should play their re-arranged league fixture in the week leading up to the semi final — which explains City’s game at Burnley last weekend — but City point out that no such principle exists in the handbook.

Even so, City argued that playing Bournemouth ahead of the cup final, on May 12, would fit with that ‘principle’. That request, though, was rejected.

Matters were complicated further by UEFA wanting to keep Wednesday, May 20 free so as to avoid a clash with the Europa League final. City had also suggested playing the Bournemouth fixture the night after that, on Thursday, May 21, to give more time for recovery following the cup final. That had appeared to be a viable option at one stage, sources say, but was ultimately rejected.

The various permutations are dizzying and give an idea of how long and complex these negotiations have been.

Regarding the Palace fixture, City had put forward last week, this week and next week as potential options.

This week and next week turned out to be incompatible with Palace’s European commitments, while last week was problematic because of Palace’s game against West Ham on Monday night.

City sources say that, at one stage, the Premier League had been open to reverting that fixture to a Sunday, so that City could play Palace last week, had they been knocked out of the FA Cup by Liverpool at the start of the month.

It leaves City with a tight schedule at the end of the season, factoring in travel down to London for the cup final against Chelsea on Saturday, May 16, a return to Manchester that evening and another journey south to Bournemouth soon after.

City have become used to playing high-stakes matches in quick succession during Pep Guardiola’s reign and, as demonstrated at Wembley for the semi-final victory over Southampton, they have a big enough squad to make changes across the competitions.

It is a far from ideal scenario for Guardiola and his players and it does make their chances of winning their remaining two competitions this season harder, though it is not beyond them to triumph anyway.

For Fantasy Premier League addicts, today’s fixture announcement represents the falling of the last scheduling domino of the season and finalises the run-in for the remainder of 2025-26.

The major headline is that we now have a confirmed double gameweek in Gameweek 36 where Crystal Palace and Manchester City will both play twice, facing each other at the Etihad Stadium just a few days after home matches against Brentford and Everton respectively.

Double Gameweek 36 will be of particular interest to FPL users looking for a golden opportunity to use any remaining chips.

Bournemouth vs. Manchester City and Chelsea vs. Tottenham Hotspur will also remain in Gameweek 37, but have a new date of Tuesday, May 19, having originally clashed with the FA Cup final.
